history.summary: A massive 3068sqft 3BR at $3.55M, only $1157 psf — but the low PSF is purely a size artifact, and the $3.55M total sits well above the liquid buyer band. Just 190m from Kembangan MRT in a small 189-unit, 2005-vintage development with only 45 URA transactions. Niche, illiquid and aging.
history.rating_rationale: For an investment hold this is the wrong risk profile despite a good location. $3.55M is far above the $1.8-2.5M deep-pool band, so the exit pool is shrunken to a handful of buyers wanting a 3000+sqft leasehold near Kembangan. Only 45 transactions (thin liquidity), a small 189-unit development, and a 2005 build (21 years old, ~78yr lease remaining) all compound exit risk. The 7.14%/yr CAGR and MRT-frontage are genuine positives that prevent an Avoid, but oversized + high-absolute-price + thin liquidity is a Neutral at best for investment.

history.summary: 189-unit D14 leasehold (2005) literally 190m from EW6 Kembangan MRT, 2BR at $1.70M / $1,790psf on 947sqft. Excellent transit access, well-maintained, bright floor-to-ceiling layouts, and a strong 7.14% URA CAGR. Asking is right on the $1,802 median (fair). Main constraint is the small 189-unit size and thin 45-txn data.
history.rating_rationale: Top-tier location — 190m covered walk to Kembangan EW6 on the East-West line — plus a strong 7.14%/yr URA and an asking price ($1,790psf) essentially at the $1,802 median means you are not overpaying. Arena score (757) and frontier status corroborate good value. The 189-unit count and 45-transaction sample are the real caveats (thinner liquidity, less reliable rate), but the unbeatable MRT proximity in a CBD-accessible corridor keeps demand broad. Solid Buy with the small-dev caveat.

history.summary: Mature 99LH 1BR near Kembangan MRT, modestly priced but with no fresh catalyst and a thin transaction base behind its headline appreciation. A fair hold, not an edge.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,471 psf vs a verified 12-mo project average ~$1,545 psf (range $952-$1,868) is only a slight discount, and age_adj_premium is just -8.7%. The standout 7.14% appreciation_pct rests on only 45 transactions, and psf_cohort_txns=2 — far too thin to trust as a forward signal under the v3.4 priors, so I discount it heavily. The 'very_old_property' flag is real: built 2005 (21 years), a 99LH with ~78 years left and accelerating lease decay, which caps forward upside. Connectivity is fine (Kembangan EWL, walkable) but it's an existing line — no dated catalyst to re-rate the unit. D14 does carry strong rental yield (3.5-4.5%), which keeps it from an Avoid, but the value gap is too small and the data too thin to call a Buy.

Headline 7.14% CAGR built on only 45 txns; psf_cohort_txns=2 — unreliable, likely data quirk
Discount to 12-mo average is small (~5%) — thin margin of safety
No new catalyst — served by an existing MRT line only
catalysts: Walkable to Kembangan MRT (East-West Line) — existing connectivity, supports rentability
D14 carries strong rental yields (3.5-4.5%) for income-focused holds
